extracted.intended_audience: NIH fellowship peer reviewers and applicants (F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing and scoring NIH fellowship (F-series) applications submitted on/after Jan 25, 2025, focusing on three restructured review criteria and related scoring/policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate's Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the candidate's academic preparation; research experience and skills; motivation and commitment to a research career; productivity and accomplishments to date; potential to contribute to the biomedical workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion aggregates prior 'Fellowship Applicant' and related considerations. Reviewers may consider varied information provided by the candidate, sponsor, and referees to determine preparedness and potential. Academic grades are no longer a component (see separate policy entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the quality of the proposed research project; appropriateness of the training environment for the proposed work; activities to address training needs; quality of the mentorship plan; and the plan to enhance reproducible research practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the rigor and feasibility of the research, alignment between project aims and training activities, clarity and substance of mentorship, and explicit plans to promote reproducibility (e.g., data/analysis sharing, robust methods). Consider whether the environment provides necessary resources and opportunities for the stated training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the sponsor's track record of mentorship; sponsor's research support and resources; institutional commitment; and career development opportunities provided to the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consolidates prior 'Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants' and 'Institutional environment and Commitment to Training' considerations into a focus on the extent of sponsor/institutional commitment to advancing the candidate's career. Emphasize concrete supports, past mentorship outcomes, and planned career development activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Score (fellowship-level assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate assessment of the likelihood the fellowship will promote the candidate's potential for, and commitment to, an independent scientific research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score synthesizes the three criteria into an overall judgment of expected career-promoting effect of the fellowship. This is distinct from the 1–9 scores assigned to each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion Scoring Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each criterion is scored 1-9 (1 = exceptional, 9 = poor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 1–9 scale to each of the three criteria; use the overall impact as a separate judgment. Use the scale consistently across applications to reflect relative merit (lower = better).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Grades Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic grades will no longer be a component of fellowship applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use transcript grades as an evaluative component of the Candidate's Preparedness and Potential criterion. Reviewers should rely on other indicators (research experience, productivity, references, statements of motivation) when assessing preparedness and potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Reference Letters and Variety of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate, sponsor, and referees may provide a variety of information for the review panel to determine the candidate's preparedness and potential; there are more detailed instructions for reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider substantive, specific information provided in reference letters consistent with updated instructions. Expect letters to address preparedness, research experience, mentorship potential, and career commitment rather than relying on grades or institutional reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias-Reduction Principle: Emphasize Commitment over Reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Review process change to reduce bias by emphasizing the commitment to the candidate without undue consideration of sponsor and institutional reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating Commitment to Candidate and other criteria, avoid overweighting sponsor or institutional prestige; focus on demonstrable mentorship record, resources, and opportunities offered to the specific candidate. The changes aim to ensure a broad range of candidates and research training contexts can be recognized as meritorious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Diverse Training Contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure a broad range of candidates and research training contexts can be recognized as meritorious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply criteria flexibly to different research settings and career stages so that nontraditional or less resourced environments with strong, appropriate training plans are not unfairly disadvantaged. Consider context-appropriate evidence of potential and training quality.
